claims.label: Source observation
claims.title: Locate Bithila and Mungthila separately
claims.text: Printed page 4 contains the two relevant contexts: §10 for Mungthila and §13 for Bithila. The source locations are checked. A new full Ahom reading is still pending, and the two passages concern different named figures.
claims.locator: Ahom-Buranji, printed p. 4, §§10 and 13 · scan page 10
claims.review: Page location checked, 23 October 2026. Name interpretation also draws on the project dossier of 10 October.

claims.label: Source observation
claims.title: The shared-throne passage is identifiable
claims.text: The passage to collate is printed page 7, §5. The historical English column describes Lengdon and Thenkham sharing a throne and consulting over government. The Ahom crop is provided so an independent reading can be checked against it.
claims.review: The source crop is checked. The historical English description is not relabelled as a fresh translation.

claims.label: Comparative evidence
claims.title: Nimi supplies a relevant royal-heaven narrative
claims.text: Jātaka 541 places Nimi at Mithilā and sends Mātali to bring him to Sakka. The journey includes moral instruction through a tour of hells and heavens. This gives a concrete narrative to compare, while the distinct purposes of the stories must remain visible.
claims.locator: Nimi Jātaka 541; the invitation and journey sections
claims.review: English primary-text translation consulted for this release. Comparison is not a claim of direct textual dependence.

claims.label: Comparative evidence
claims.title: The motif does not identify Nimi uniquely
claims.text: The project’s source audit also compares Sādhina Jātaka 494, another Mithilā king’s encounter with Sakka, including shared sovereignty. A shared seat or heavenly host needs to be tested against this wider narrative tradition.
claims.locator: Sādhina Jātaka 494; project audit, 10 October 2026, pp. 4–5
claims.review: Alternative comparison retained to avoid treating a widely shared motif as unique evidence.

claims.label: Manuscript lead
claims.title: An Ahom Nemi witness strengthens the research question
claims.text: The earlier audit identifies Nemi Mang in the EAP catalogue and records alternative copying dates within the Ahom monarchy. A catalogue identification supports a manuscript lead; it does not establish the date of the story’s first arrival or name a royal patron.
claims.review: Inherited catalogue finding. Live verification and a new colophon reading remain pending.

claims.label: Open hypothesis
claims.title: Buddhist adaptation is plausible; the exact route remains open
claims.text: The place-name correspondences, royal-heaven motif and Nemi witness make Buddhist adaptation a serious question. They do not yet demonstrate that the complete Lengdon foundation story derives exclusively from Nimi, or that every Ahom ruler practised Buddhism.
claims.locator: Synthesis from the project’s 10 October 2026 source audit
claims.review: Research inference, not a certified translation or a settled historical conclusion.
